draft.title: Solving trigonometric equations
card: First rearrange to get one trig ratio alone. For 2 sin x = 1, divide by 2 to get sin x = 1/2.
Find the related acute angle by ignoring the sign. Here sin 30° = 1/2, so the related angle is 30°.

Use the signs in each quadrant to place the angle. Sin is positive in quadrants 1 and 2, so x = 30° and x = 180° − 30° = 150°. Cos is positive in quadrants 1 and 4. Tan is positive in quadrants 1 and 3.
To find every solution in a larger domain, add or subtract the period: 360° for sin and cos, 180° for tan. For 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°, the solutions of sin x = 1/2 are 30° and 150°.
draft.remember: Find the related angle, place it using the quadrants, then use the period for the rest of the domain.

a.q: What are the solutions of 2 cos x = 1 for 0° ≤ x ≤ 360°?
a.why: cos x = 1/2, so the related angle is 60°. Cos is positive in quadrants 1 and 4, giving 60° and 360° − 60° = 300°. The pair 60° and 120° uses the quadrants where sin is positive, which is the wrong ratio.
a.clue: Cos is positive in quadrants 1 and 4.

b.q: How many solutions does tan x = 1 have for 0° ≤ x ≤ 720°?
b.why: The related angle is 45°, and tan has a period of 180°. The solutions are 45°, 225°, 405° and 585°, so there are 4. Using a period of 360° gives only 2, which is the tempting mistake.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: cos x = 1/2 gives 60° and 300°, and tan x = 1 has 4 solutions (45°, 225°, 405°, 585°) in 0° to 720°.
